Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the StratoCloud Q3 FY24 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star then one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing StratoCloud's results for the Q3 FY24. With me on the call are Jamie Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; Lisa Moreno, Chief Product Officer; Mike Thompson, Chief Marketing Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Sales Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Security Officer; and Nina Kaur, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jamie Chen.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. StratoCloud delivered exceptional results for the Q3 FY24, demonstrating the strength of our cloud platform and the increasing demand for our AI-driven solutions across diverse industries.

During the quarter, we focused on eight key strategic priorities:
1. Expanding our global reach through strategic partnerships.
2. Driving innovation in edge computing and IoT solutions.
3. Enhancing our commitment to open source technologies.
4. Strengthening our data privacy and compliance programs.
5. Investing in our employees' professional development.
6. Improving our operational efficiency through automation.
7. Fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.
8. Accelerating the adoption of sustainable cloud practices.

Let me highlight our standout progress in AI/ML workload growth and adoption rates, which have become central to our momentum. In Q3 FY24, total revenue reached $28.7 billion, up 32% year-over-year, with cloud revenue at $26.2 billion accelerating to 35% YoY growth. Operating income hit a record $11.4 billion at a 42% margin, largely propelled by explosive AI/ML demand. AI/ML workloads accounted for 28% of our total cloud compute consumption, up from 18% a year ago and more than doubling from Q2.

Our AI/ML compute hours billed surged 145% YoY to 4.2 trillion hours, outpacing core IaaS growth. Training workloads, at 62% of usage, grew 130% YoY from foundation model pre-training and fine-tuning, while inference accelerated 168% YoY to 1.6 trillion hours—offering 15-20 margin points above training due to efficient batching and lower GPU times. Enterprise adoption among Fortune 500 customers reached 78%, up from 52% last year, including 95% of top global banks and 85% of major tech firms. SMB and mid-market hit 45%, doubled YoY, thanks to our pay-as-you-go ML Studio for easy fine-tuning of models like Llama 3 or Mistral. We now have 1.2 million active AI/ML users, with net retention at 142%.

Key trends include multi-modality, with 40% of new workloads using vision-language models via our ForgeVision API equivalent, boosting sectors like autonomous vehicles and healthcare imaging—running 500 petaflop-days weekly on our clusters. Agentic AI and RAG pipelines exploded 210% YoY, powered by our VectorForge database for 10x faster hybrid search.

Technically, our ForgeCore AI accelerators power 35% of training, with 4x better price-performance than H100s for FP8, deployed across 12 new zones with HyperCluster for 1.8 trillion-parameter models. ForgeBedrock 2.0 optimizes inference with vLLM or TensorRT-LLM, cutting latency 60% and TTFT under 200ms. Our open-sourced QuantumLoRA toolkit has 50k GitHub forks, driving ecosystem growth.

Regionally, North America saw AI/ML drive 48% of cloud growth at 62% YoY compute expansion, insulated by sovereign deals like $5B U.S. DoD FedRAMP AI. EMEA grew 55% YoY, with GDPR-compliant fine-tuning and OVHcloud edge partnerships capturing 25% auto AI share. APAC blazed at 72% YoY, led by Japan and India; Hong Kong grew 90% despite China regs. LatAm/MEA showed 35% adoption gains.

Strategically, AI ARR jumped 180% to $18.5B, RPO $52B mostly multi-year, with 65% POC-to-production via AI Escape Hatch migrations. Partnerships with NVIDIA (28% DGX Q2 output), AMD, and sustainability via liquid cooling and carbon-aware scheduling position us strongly. We guide Q4 AI/ML compute to 150-160% YoY, with inference leading, targeting 30%+ of $200B+ AI cloud TAM by 2027.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Patel to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Sarah Patel:
Thank you, Jamie. We are very pleased with our financial results for the Q3 FY24. Revenue increased by 28% year-over-year to $28.7 billion, exceeding our guidance for the quarter. Our gross margin was 72.1%, driven by our efficient cost management and economies of scale. Our operating margin was 32%.

I'm thrilled to walk you through our overall financial performance highlights, underscoring our leadership in hyperscale cloud computing. Driven by AI/ML workloads, sovereign cloud, and hybrid multi-cloud, we set records across metrics.

Total revenue hit $28.7 billion, topping guidance with 28% YoY and 8% QoQ growth, outpacing IDC's 21% cloud market estimate. IaaS led at $18.1 billion or 63%, up 28% YoY on GPU compute for genAI, with H100/A100 utilization up 150% for top customers. PaaS reached $7.0 billion, 24% up, powering 45% new AI deployments; Kubernetes services grew 35% amid VMware shifts. SaaS/other added $3.6 billion, 13% up, with AetherGuard zero-trust hitting 10,000 customers amid ransomware and compliance.

ARR expanded to $110 billion, 26% YoY; RPO $182 billion, 32% up, 95% billable next year—from U.S. bank sovereign cloud and European automaker sims. NRR steady 128%, adding 1,200 net customers including 45 $100M+ whales, totaling 85,000 enterprises.

Profitability scaled: GAAP gross margin 72.1% up 140bps on 92% data center utilization and PaaS mix. Non-GAAP op margin 32%, up 300bps despite $4.2B capex for AI DCs. Net income $8.7B or $2.10 EPS, up 28%; FCF $9.9B or 34.5% revenue, funding $5.8B buybacks/dividends. Balance sheet strong: $83B cash, 0.8x net debt/EBITDA.

Regionally balanced: Americas $14.9B (52%), 26% up on public sector 40% growth vs. AWS/Azure pricing—we offered 20% deeper discounts. EMEA $8.0B (28%), 28% up; sovereign zones $1.4B run-rate under EU Data Act. APAC $5.8B (20%), 20% up, Japan/India 36%/46% on 5G/TSMC.

GenAI boom drove 45% AI/ML expansion to 22% revenue; 50,000+ Blackwell GPUs deployed, AetherInfer cutting latency 40%. Cloud Everywhere: 12 edge DCs for 5G MEC, AetherFabric multi-cloud integrations (15% hybrid share), 55% renewables.

Positioned for $800B TAM at 23% CAGR; capex raised to $18-20B FY24, ROIC >25%. Risks: GPU chains, export controls—mitigated by AMD/Intel.

For Q4, revenue $29.5-30.0B (25-27% YoY), op income $9.7-9.9B. FY24 $114-115B.

Next, I'd like to introduce Raj Singh, who will provide an update on our technology strategy and roadmap.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Sarah. We are committed to leading the way in cloud technology innovation. We are making significant investments in research and development to create cutting-edge solutions for our customers.

As we power the intelligent cloud, compute and storage capacity utilization rates are key to our efficiency, margins, and demand fulfillment for AI and migrations. In Q3 FY24, overall compute utilization hit 82.3%, up 450bps YoY and 210bps QoQ—our highest in three years.

CPU compute averaged 79.1% for VMs/K8s via Aether Compute Engine; GPU/accelerators 91.7% first time over 90%, with 60% GPU for Llama 3 training/fine-tunes. Storage blended 76.8% up 380bps: block 81.2%, object 74.5%, archive 62.4%. Excludes 10-15% spot buffers; PUE 1.18.

YoY compute from 77.9%, storage 73%, driven by 28% AI growth; sequential 5-7% upticks. Inference now 55% GPU, extending job durations 20% QoQ.

Regional: NA 84.6% compute/79.2% storage (N.Va/Oregon 87%+ GPUs); EMEA 80.1%/74.8% (Frankfurt/Paris sovereign); APAC 78.9%/72.3% (Tokyo/Singapore 85%); LatAm/other 75.4%.

Initiatives: Liquid Cooling 2.0 on 40% racks boosts density 1.5x, +8-10% util; Aether Capacity Optimizer reclaims 12%; reserved capacity 35% fleet. Storage erasure coding 1.1:1 ratio +5%; Aether Flex NVMe-oF 2M IOPS, 92% adoption.

Targeting 85% blended YE: AI supply chain w/TSMC/Samsung <90-day GPUs; 50 edge micro-DCs; dynamic spot 65% discounts 25% uptake; carbon-neutral premiums.

Q4 guide: compute 83-85%, storage 77-79%. Setting pace in AI cloud.

Now, I'll pass it over to Lisa Moreno to discuss our product roadmap and recent launches.

Lisa Moreno:
Thank you, Raj. We recently launched StratoAI Inference Engine, a groundbreaking solution designed to revolutionize real-time AI applications.

Today, I'd like to discuss our new service launches and phenomenal market reception amid genAI, edge, and sovereign demands. Our Q1 flagship StratoAI Inference Engine, on NitroForge Arm-based architecture (40% lower TCO than x86), integrates TensorFlow/PyTorch/Hugging Face. Over 12,000 customers activated Q-o-Q 250% ramp, $185M new ARR; 35% AI compute growth.

MLPerf v3.1: 22% faster than AWS Inferentia, 18% better price-perf than GCP TPUs. NPS 78 via auto-scaling tokens. Wins: $50M bank fraud, NVIDIA H100 passthrough.

Q2 StratoEdge Sovereign for regulated industries: geo-fenced AMD SEV-SNP enclaves, StratoKube hybrid K8s, WireGuard zero-trust. $92M ARR EMEA, 60% fin/health; 28% APAC sovereign share.

New services 22% RPO, 36-month contracts.

Regions: NA 55% (multi-cloud 62% per Gartner); EMEA 25% 180% sovereign; APAC 15% 120%; RoW 5%.

$2.5B sustainable infra (PUE<1.15), carbon-aware; 45% deals ESG. New services 35-40% Q4 growth, 72% margins.

Redefining cloud economics.

I'll now hand it over to Mike Thompson to provide an update on our marketing initiatives and brand strategy.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Lisa. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and driving demand for our innovative solutions.

As we build awareness, let's examine cloud services revenue growth drivers, QoQ and YoY changes—our core engine. Cloud services hit $26.4 billion, 18% QoQ from Q1's $22.4B, 37% YoY from Q2 FY23's $19.3B—12th straight accelerating quarter, topping Synergy's 25% market.

Customer momentum: 1,200 new incl. 45 F500 (U.S. bank StratoCompute, automaker StratoAI); NRR 128%, 25% QoQ expansions; RPO $145B +42% YoY, current $52B +28%.

IaaS $14.2B, 20% QoQ/41% YoY; GPU 92% util, 50k H100/A100, 150% AI training QoQ. PaaS $8.1B 16%/34%; StratoLambda 4.2T invocations +60%, StratoEKS 35% containers, databases +22%. SaaS $4.1B 14%/30%.

Regions: Americas $14.5B 55% 19%/39% (FedRAMP DoD); EMEA $6.8B 26% 17%/36% (Frankfurt/Paris sovereign); APAC $5.1B 19% 21%/35% (Mumbai 5G).

Initiatives: StratoInferentia 2.0 40% cheaper inference; 65% renewables -18% carbon; hybrid w/VMware/OpenShift 15% $15B market. $12B H2 capex 20 AZs; 72% margins.

Q4 guide $27.8-28.2B, 15-17% QoQ 35%+ YoY.

Next, I'd like to introduce Elena Vasquez, who will discuss our sales performance and customer acquisition strategies.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. Our sales team has been instrumental in driving our strong growth in the Q3 FY24. We are focused on expanding our customer base and strengthening our existing relationships.

Diving into new customer acquisition cost—or CAC—analysis, a key go-to-market efficiency indicator vs. hyperscalers. CAC covers sales/marketing—commissions, partners, ads, events, free credits, pilots—divided by new customers. Our SaaS model: high upfront offset by 128% NRR expansions, >5x LTV/CAC, <18mo payback.

Q3 blended CAC $42,800, 15% YoY down from $50,400, seq from $44,200—sixth straight quarter below Gartner $55-65k benchmark.

Cohorts: Enterprise >$1M ARR $128,500 -18% YoY (62% new ARR, $2.7M TCV, 6.1mo cycles); Mid $28,400 -12% (45% self-serve Nebula); SMB <$100k $4,200 flat 3x vol (1M vCPU/5TB free).

LTV/CAC 10.2x up from 8.7x (5yr life, 20% churn, 130% NRR); payback 14.7mo.

Drivers: Inbound 68% opps +16% (150+ deep-dives Kubernetes/Polaris, 180% SEO); PLG free tier 22% 90-day paid double avg, -25% SMB CAC; partners 42% logos $31k CAC vs $52k direct (1,200+ Marketplace Snowflake/Databricks, $150M consultancy); sales ramp 4.2mo, 92% attainment, AI lead scoring; virtual Cloud Next 45k 4.8x ROI.

Regions: NA 65% ARR $38.9k -20% (75% RFP wins, AI OpenAI-like); EMEA 18% $52.3k -8% (GDPR sovereign €200M public); APAC 12% $61.4k -5% (Alibaba rival, India 3x Jio); LATAM 5% $47.2k Brazil fintech.

Future: StratoProspect LLM 28% CAC cut; StratoHybrid 90% F100; $500M edge PoPs. Prioritize fin/health high-LTV. Q4 $41-43k, FY24 ~$43.5k -14%, FY26 <$35k PLG/partners. $1.2B FY24 FCF.

Now, I'll pass it over to Tom Reilly to discuss our security initiatives and commitment to data protection.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Elena. Security is paramount to our mission. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and ensuring the integrity of our cloud platform.

As we outline key assumptions underlying revenue and profitability forecasts for FY24/FY25, these are based on trends, pipeline, macros, Gartner/IDC/Synergy. FY24 $114B 26% growth, 32% margins +200bps; FY25 $66B 27% growth 35% margins—no recession, stable rates.

Revenue: 78% IaaS/PaaS +28%, ARPA +12%; AI/ML 35% compute FY25 (+45% GPU CAGR, 90% util, 150MW capacity); 1-2% price erosion offset 15% vol; storage +22% 18% EB $0.023/GB. SaaS 32% $4.2B Bedrock-like 40% attach $1.2M MACV, edge $1.1B 25% IoT/5G. NRR 118%, 3% churn 20% expansion, 2,500 $1M logos 45% conv. IDC $679B cloud 22%, 89% multi-cloud.

Profit: Capex 14% rev, FCF 28%; PUE 1.25 +5%, $0.45/kWh, Graviton 30% TCO; OpEx S&M 22% R&D 14% G&A 5%, headcount +8% 145k. Deprec $11B.

Regions: NA 60% 22%, CHIPS $2B; EMEA 25% 30% EU Data €5B; APAC 10% 40% India; LatAm 5% 35%.

Macro: GDP>2%, IT +8% 70% cloud. Tech: Quantum Network/zero-trust 25% premium. Sustain: 100% renewable.

Upside: AI capex, multi-cloud 28% share. Downside: pricing, GPUs (6mo buffer), antitrust. Outpace peers.

Finally, I'd like to introduce Nina Kaur, who will share insights into our innovation strategy and future growth opportunities.

Nina Kaur:
Thank you, Tom. We are constantly exploring new technologies and business models to drive innovation and create value for our customers.

I'll now turn to our Q3 FY24 results and outlook for Q4/FY25. Revenue $28.7B +28% YoY/30% cc, compute/storage +45% >cloud market. RPO $182B +35%, current $72B +42%; SaaS ARR $18.5B +22%; $500M+ F100 multi-year.

Q4 revenue $28.0-28.5B, 26-29% YoY/28-31% cc, $400M seasonality.

Segments: IaaS $17.2-17.6B 62% +32% Graviton4/AI Trainium3 60% adoption 85% util 45 AZs. PaaS $6.8-7.0B +24% EKS 2M clusters Lambda 15T +40%, Bedrock AI 200+ ISVs. SaaS $4.0-4.1B +20% Workspaces $450M ARR Sovereign.

Geography: Americas $14.6-14.8B 52% +30% DoD $1.2B; EMEA $7.3-7.4B 26% +25% Frankfurt/Paris AI +55%; APAC $6.1-6.3B 22% +28% India 2x Mumbai/Jio.

Op margins 32-33% $2.1B opts PUE 1.15.

FY25 $115.5-118.0B +24-27% >prior.

Mid $116.75B: IaaS $72B 62% +31% $10B capex H200/Inferentia2 50%+ AI; PaaS $28.5B 24% +26% SageMaker 100+ models 35% attach +18% ARPU; SaaS $16B 14% +22% GuardDuty Quantum preview 25% NRR.

APAC 30%, Americas 28%. AI 40% pipeline, 1.2ZB storage 11 9s; 65% F500 50%+ SAP/Oracle/VMware cloud-native; free egress Snowflake/Databricks Azure parity; carbon-neutral 2026.

Risks: HBM GPUs ($5B silicon), trade. FY25 op inc $41-43B FCF $35B+. $500B TTM in 3yrs >20% CAGR.

Back to Jamie Chen.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term sustainable growth.

Operator:
Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks for taking my question. Can you provide more color on the key assumptions behind your FY25 revenue acceleration and any macro sensitivities?

Jamie Chen:
Thanks, John. Our FY25 guide assumes continued AI tailwinds with 35% of compute from AI/ML, stable pricing erosion at 1-2%, and NRR around 118% from expansions. Macro-wise, we model US GDP over 2%, no recession, and IT budgets up 8% with 70% to cloud. Upside from extra Big Tech AI capex; downside from deeper pricing wars or GPU delays, but our buffers and diversification keep us on track for the midpoint. We're executing well against these.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. On CAC, how sustainable is the compression, and what role does PLG play in Q4 guidance?

Sarah Patel:
Thanks, Emily. The 15% YoY CAC drop to $42.8k is sustainable via inbound at 68%, PLG converting 22% free tier users, and partners at 42% logos. PLG slashed SMB CAC 25%, and we'll hit 50% mix long-term. Q4 guide $41-43k factors this, with StratoProspect AI adding more efficiency. Unit economics strong at 10x LTV/CAC.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Thank you. Nina, with AI adoption at 78% F500, what's the biggest opportunity in innovation for next year?

Nina Kaur:
David, thanks. The shift to inference and agentic AI is huge—guiding 150%+ compute growth Q4. Our Bedrock-like studio and multi-model support position us for 50% AI revenue growth FY25, especially multi-cloud escapes from Azure/SageMaker. Partnerships and custom silicon will capture more of the $200B TAM.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim:
Hi, thanks. Raj, utilization hit 91% on GPUs—any capacity concerns heading into peak AI demand?

Raj Singh:
Rachel, great question. 82% blended compute is solid, with GPUs at 91.7% thanks to liquid cooling and optimizers reclaiming 12%. We're guiding 83-85% Q4, with $10B+ capex adding zones and edge. Supply diversified beyond NVIDIA; no major constraints expected.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions and your continued interest in StratoCloud.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
